To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the connectionist approach to the simulation of logic programming is possible and (ii) learning algorithms can be applied to the construction of connectionist neural networks for the simulation of deductive algorithms in conventional logic programming.

(1) learning algorithms recognised in the field of neurocomputing can serve as a foundation for building neural networks that simulate logic programs with uncertainty; (2) learning algorithms can be used to build neural networks that simulate SLD-resolution algorithm.
learning and deduction in logic and neural network are two different ways of achieving the same goal, i.e., to find the solution to a given problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) to develop a connectionist model of logic program with uncertainty and conventional SLD-resolution algorithm; (2) to develop a neural network for learning the semantics of logic programs; (3) to investigate the interplay between the connectionist model and learning algorithm; (4) to demonstrate the feasibility of the approach by means of computer simulation.
the development of neural networks that can simulate the work of deductive algorithms in the field of logic and reasoning.
the development of new techniques for the construction of connectionist neural networks, which can be used to simulate logic program reasoning with uncertainty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neural networks are not only capable of learning, but also of deducting, and that they can be used as a tool to simulate the work of logic programming.
the neural network is able to learn and simulate the deductive algorithm of logic programs with uncertainty.
the connectionist approach is a promising and useful tool in the development of logic-based systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
learning and deductive methods in neural networks and logic are complementary and they can be used together to build intelligent systems.

we have developed a connectionist model for logic programs with uncertainties and we have shown how the learning algorithm of the connectionist model can be used to simulate the work of SLD-resolution.

learning and deductive algorithm in logic and neural network can work together and complement each other in the sense that the learning algorithm can be used to construct a neural network which is capable of simulating the work of deductive algorithm in the logic program.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the learning algorithms in neural networks are not just a way to train the network to perform a certain task, but they can also be used to simulate the work of logical operators.
the learning algorithms are not just for training neural networks but they can be used for deductive inference in logic.

the learning algorithms can be used to build neural networks which are capable of simulating the work of semantic operators for logic programs with uncertainties and conventional algorithms of SLD- resolution.
